faqs.a: Enlisted Marines must be 17 to 28 years old, the strictest age cap of any U.S. service branch. Those under 18 need parental consent. While the Army, Navy, and Air Force raised their maximums to 41 or 42 between 2024 and 2026, the Marine Corps kept its limit at 28 to preserve its elite fighting force identity.
faqs.q: What is the Marine Corps age limit in 2026?

faqs.a: Every recruit must pass the Initial Strength Test: pull-ups or push-ups, a plank hold, and a 1.5-mile run. Standards vary by age and gender, but failing any event sends you back for more training before boot camp. Fitness is central to Marine identity, so recruiters expect candidates to train before shipping out.
faqs.q: What is the Initial Strength Test?

faqs.a: Yes, lawful permanent residents (green card holders) can enlist, but only U.S. citizens can become officers. Enlisted Marines also need a high school diploma, though GED holders can qualify with higher ASVAB scores. Felony convictions generally disqualify applicants from all branches.
faqs.q: Can green card holders join the Marine Corps?

faqs.a: Boot camp lasts 13 weeks at Marine Corps Recruit Depot Parris Island in South Carolina or San Diego, California. It is the longest enlisted basic training in the U.S. military and is famous for its intensity, drill instructors, and the final 54-hour crucible exercise that tests everything recruits learned.
faqs.q: How long is Marine Corps boot camp?

faqs.a: Officers need a bachelor's degree, U.S. citizenship, and must be 18 to 28 at commissioning. The main routes are Officer Candidates School in Quantico, Virginia (10 weeks), the Platoon Leaders Class, NROTC programs, and the U.S. Naval Academy in Annapolis. Candidates also need an AFQT score of 74, or ACT 22, or SAT 1000.
faqs.q: How do you become a Marine officer in 2026?

headline: Joining the U.S. Marine Corps: Requirements and Paths in 2026
metaDescription: Marine Corps recruitment 2026: age 17-28 limit, Initial Strength Test, 13-week boot camp, ASVAB AFQT 74 for officers, and officer routes via OCS and Annapolis

sections.content:
The Marine Corps, founded on 10 November 1775 and part of the Department of the Navy, is America's expeditionary fighting force. Marines guard embassies and naval bases and serve as the nation's amphibious and global strike force, known for being first to fight.

In 2026 it keeps the strictest entry rules of any branch. Enlisted Marines must be 17 to 28 years old, need a high school diploma or equivalent, and must have no felony convictions. While other branches raised their age caps to 41 or 42 in 2024-2026, the Marines deliberately held the line at 28.
sections.title: The Corps and its strict entry rules

sections.content:
Every applicant must pass the Initial Strength Test before shipping to boot camp: pull-ups or push-ups, a timed plank, and a 1.5-mile run. Minimum standards depend on age and gender, but the message is clear: Marines expect candidates to arrive already fit.

Physical fitness is woven into Marine culture more than any other branch. Recruits who fail an event are sent back to train before they can leave for boot camp, and fitness testing continues throughout a Marine's career with annual physical and combat fitness tests.
sections.title: Fitness: the Initial Strength Test

sections.content:
Officers must be U.S. citizens aged 18 to 28 at commissioning and hold a bachelor's degree. They need an AFQT score of 74 on the ASVAB, or an ACT score of 22, or an SAT score of 1000. The academic bar is intentionally high for future leaders.

The main route is the 10-week Officer Candidates School at Quantico, Virginia, alongside alternatives like the Platoon Leaders Class, NROTC scholarships, and the U.S. Naval Academy at Annapolis. Each path ends with the same commission as a second lieutenant.
